panels.rationale: Gross pathology image of excised subcutaneous specimen demonstrating calcified guinea worms, which is a direct manifestation of dracunculiasis as stated in the caption and supported by the article title.
panels.attribution_text: Athavale et al. Guinea Worm Disease Presenting as a Subcutaneous Calcification.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.62733. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Circled areas in excised specimen showing calcified guinea worms
in_text_mentions: On ultrasonography (USG), the subcutaneous foreign body of calcifications was noted in the subcutaneous plane in the right hip region. Soft tissue appeared normal, there was no evidence of fluid in tissue or tendons or soft tissue oedema. After obtaining the consent of the patient, excision and excision of multiple subcutaneous calcifications was planned under spinal anaesthesia and the excised specimen was sent for histopathology examination for definitive diagnosis (Figure 3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Anteroposterior hip radiograph from a patient with confirmed dracunculiasis, showing classic calcified subcutaneous worm tracks as described in the article title and caption, with no features of other diseases or non-patient content. B: Lateral hip radiograph from the same patient with confirmed dracunculiasis, showing the same classic calcified subcutaneous worm tracks as the AP view, with no features of other diseases or non-patient content.

panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E histology image from a case report focused on dracunculiasis (Guinea Worm Disease) presenting as subcutaneous calcification. The image depicts the excised patient specimen, with circled areas showing necrotic tissue and eosinophilic calcified lesions consistent with a calcifying parasitic granuloma associated with dead dracunculiasis worm. No excluded content (diagrams, other disease, controls, etc.) is present, so the panel qualifies for inclusion in the clinical diagnosis library.
panels.attribution_text: Athavale et al. Guinea Worm Disease Presenting as a Subcutaneous Calcification.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.62733. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Circled areas in the histopathology specimen showing dead necrotic tissue with eosinophilic calcified lesions
in_text_mentions: Surgical excision of the subcutaneous calcifications was done under spinal anaesthesia and the excised specimen was sent for histopathological examination for definitive diagnosis (Figures 5-7).
